threads_text: OpenAI cut its funding round target by $10 billion to about $20 billion, and its target valuation fell to $1.25 trillion, the FT reports. It happened the same day the Nasdaq dropped 2.9%. Are investors finally getting nervous about AI?

paragraphs.text: OpenAI has cut the target for its latest funding round by $10 billion and is now looking to raise about $20 billion, according to a Financial Times report published on October 30, 2026, and relayed by Reuters. The company's desired valuation has also dropped to $1.25 trillion, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.

The round had been pitched at $30 billion. OpenAI first sought a $1.4 trillion valuation in September and had already lowered that figure to $1.25 trillion earlier in October after pushback from some investors, The Next Web reported on October 25, citing the Financial Times, CNBC and Bloomberg.

OpenAI set a Friday deadline for investors to commit, according to Reuters. The first close of the round is expected to bring in less than $20 billion because some investors reduced their allocations. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that OpenAI had raised less than half of its original $30 billion target, according to a summary of that report by FourWeekMBA, which noted the exact amount raised was not given.

A consortium of investors based in the United Arab Emirates, including the state-backed technology fund MGX, is expected to be the largest participant, Reuters reported. As part of that arrangement, OpenAI would gain an option to lease newly developed computing capacity in the region. Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz are also expected to take part.

Wealthy individuals will be offered the chance to invest later through a retail offering at the $1.25 trillion valuation, according to the report. OpenAI, MGX, Coatue, Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and Founders Fund could not be reached, Reuters said.
A rough week for AI stocks

The cut came during a sharp selloff in technology shares. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on Friday, October 30, and closed 7.8% below its record close of October 6, as investors worried about heavy spending on artificial intelligence, Reuters reported.

OpenAI is pursuing a stock market listing in 2027. It had been keen to close the round partly to get ahead of Anthropic's expected listing, because the two companies are drawing on a similar pool of investors, according to Reuters. The Next Web reported that investors expect Anthropic to go public in November. OpenAI last raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion valuation, according to The Next Web.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the smaller round says more about investor appetite than about OpenAI's business. About $20 billion is still a very large sum, but the trimmed allocations suggest that even the best-known AI company is not immune to the market's new questions about when AI spending will pay off. The timing also puts OpenAI and Anthropic in direct competition for the same large checks.
The next signal to watch is the final size of the first close and how Anthropic's listing is priced, since both will show how much money investors are still willing to put into frontier AI labs.
